sourceMaterials.text:
A Raptor style full flow rocket engine on a test stand

Throat and exit are measured from the model (area ratio 31), so the nozzle solution gives Mach 4.06 at the exit and, at full power (330 bar), 2,462 kN and Isp 321 s at sea level.

Cut the regen cooling and the copper throat melts in milliseconds. The flame turns green: that is the engine burning its own copper.

Throw a fan blade and it tells you the load the case has to hold.

sourceMaterials.text:
Machine Skill by Airsup


















  
  



  
  
    Name a machine. Claude builds the real thing.

    
      Machine Skill, by Airsup: an open source skill for Claude Code. One line in, a photoreal simulation out: real dimensions, real materials, moving on real physics, in a single HTML file. Plus the film to post it.

      npx skills add AirsupHQ/machine-skillCopy

      Source on GitHubOpen a machineThe factory skill

    

  
  

  Every frame is three.js in a browser, recorded by the skill's own script. Every number on screen comes from a solver.


  
    Each from a single line

    Type the line under a machine into Claude Code and you get a page like this one. Open it: drag the slider, cut it open, take it apart, break it. More machines are on the way.

    

  

  
    How it works

    The skill is a SKILL.md Claude reads, a small runtime every page inlines, and a recorder. No build step, no dependencies beyond three.js from a pinned CDN.

    
      01
Research
Claude writes down the real dimensions, the parts in assembly order, the 3 to 6 equations that make the machine work, the number you care about and the failure an engineer worries about.


      02
Build
Closed solids at real size: lathe turned parts, twisted airfoils, involute gears, routed pipes, bolt circles. Measured metals, paints and glass on a softbox studio set.


      03
Solve
A small honest model runs every frame and drives every motion and number: a Brayton cycle, a nozzle solution, slider crank kinematics, a pump curve against a heartbeat.


      04
Film
One command records a 28 second film in numbered beats: the line typed, the machine assembling, the solver running, the cutaway, the break. Music bed included.


    

  

  
    Inside every page

    
      Cutaway with real section facesEvery part is a closed solid; the shader draws the cut faces at the plane, so a section can sweep in live.

      Explode, x-ray, slow motionParts move apart on their assembly axes; casings turn to glass while the core keeps running.

      Break itThe solver decides what fails: a fan blade's imbalance load, a copper throat melting, valves floating past the redline.

      Live labelsPinned to the section planes, carrying the solver's values: pressures, temperatures, flows, speeds.

      How it is computedEvery page shows its model in plain words and the equations exactly as the code solves them.

      Film modeA deterministic clock, a cursor that drags and clicks, beat captions, and a recorder that refuses magenta frames.

    

  

  
    MIT licensed. Built with Claude Opus 5.5 by Airsup, from the machines in airsup.ai/lab.

    Sibling: the factory skill. Inspired by Anatomy.
